To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have identified two novel monoclonal anti-murine antibodies that recognize distinct intestinal epithelial cell subpopulations and that these antibodies can be used in combination to isolate and investigate Lgr5+ and Bmi1+ intestinal stem cells.

we have developed a new set of antibodies to study intestinal stem cell biology, and that these antibodies reveal dynamic plasticity between Lgr5- expressing and Bmi1-expressing intestinal cell populations.
Lgr5+ and Bmi1+ stem cells are functionally plastic, as demonstrated by the ability of each to generate the other in 3-dimensional ex vivo culture.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification, isolation and analysis of intestinal epithelial cell populations that contribute to the renewal of the intestinal lining.
the intestinal stem cell (SC) and its role in tissue homeostasis and regeneration.
the development of novel reagents and methods to study stem cell populations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Lgr5+ ISCs are the primary ISC population in homeostasis and during regenerative epithelium repair and are the primary source of the Bmi1+ cell population.
the two populations are not mutually exclusive and can be in a state of plasticity.
Lgr5+ ISCs are not necessarily the only stem cell population that can give rise to Bmi+ stem cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified novel monoclonal antibody reagents that allow us to identify and isolate two different stem cell populations in the intestine.

the intestinal stem cell populations are more dynamic than previously appreciated and that the Lgr5+ and Bmi1+ cells are in fact plastic and can be interconverted depending on the physiological context.
we have developed new monoclonal antibodies to the intestinal epitheliam that we have used to study the interactions between two different stem cell populations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a dynamic plasticity between Lgr5 and Bmi1-expressing cells.
Lgr5 and Bmi1 are not necessarily mutually exclusive.
Lgr5GPF+ cells are able to give rise to Bmi-1+ cells and that Bmi-1GFP+ cells can give rise to Lgr5GFF+ cells in the intestine.
